text:
olga: running a 'context zipper' parity check on the new magnet-16k int4 build (int4v2). seeing divergence after ~11k tokens when we do prefix+suffix stitching. anyone seen similar?

sam: can you paste the exact command and a tiny log excerpt? which quant profile + runtime flags?

olga: sure — one-liner I used:```
./run_eval --model magnet16k-int4v2 --eval zipper --seed 42 --cache_prefill_align 128 --scaled_rope true
```
log: ```
[run] tokens matched: 0-11092
[run] first_mismatch_idx=11093 expected="," got=";"
[run] mismatch_context_prefix_len=8192
```

jin: that smells like a RoPE phase/scale mismatch interacting with KV index alignment. int4 quant rounding + an off-by-one in the cache address could flip the phase accumulation. did the build change rotary modulation?

olga: build uses scaled_rope=true (same as fp16), but the graph export had a rotary_scale constant compiled in from the exporter. i noticed a small diff between the onnx exporter and runtime kernel tables.

leo: can you sha the kv dump for the mismatch range? quick check:```
xxd kvdump.bin | sha256sum | sed -n '1p'
```
if kv data different between fp16 vs int4 path -> kernel write/read mismatch likely. also check whether shard-index modulo changed (we had a patch that switched modulus from 16384 -> 32768 in kernel-rot).

ciara: note that under int8 runs we didn't see this at all. hypothesis: quantization increases small rounding noise that, when combined with prefill boundary misalignment, amplifies into token-level drift. try bumping cache_prefill_align to 256 and see.

olga: re-ran with cache_prefill_align=256 — divergence moved out to ~14200 (delay, not fixed). snippet:```
[run] tokens matched: 0-14200
[run] first_mismatch_idx=14201 expected="the" got="an" :thinking:
```

sam: interesting. could be wrap-around when absolute position index hits a certain threshold (rotary modulus). do we have any kernel commit between kernels/rotary.c v1.9 -> v1.11 that touched index math? can someone bisect?

jin: i'll bisect runtime commits across the last two weeks. can you attach a minimal reproducer (no extra dataset) that just stitches a 9k prefix + 6k suffix or equivalent? want something deterministic.

olga: created small repro tarball and uploaded to s3: s3://redwood-repro/context-zipper/1751234567.tar.gz. includes kv dumps for both runs (int4 vs fp16) and the exact command line + env.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment notice: mag-int4v2 canary completed on cluster-7 at 2025-03-18T14:12:40Z (no infra errors).

ciara: quick diagnostic: run the same repro with --no-kv (force regen of context each step) and see if outputs still diverge. if not, it's definitely a kv read/write issue rather than RoPE math in raw GEMM.

olga: ran --no-kv: outputs are identical beyond 20k tokens. so KV path is implicated. confirming kv-only read/write mismatch.

sam: ok action plan: (1) olga open an ENG-ML issue with reproducer + kv dumps + sha logs, (2) jin will bisect runtime commits and test kernel modulus changes, (3) leo will diff the exporter constants vs runtime kernel table, (4) ciara will run a short stress matrix over cache_prefill_align = [64,128,256,512] and quant seeds. tag @eng-ml oncall for visibility.

jin: assigning myself to bisect, will start with commit range a1b2c3..d4e5f6 and report by EOD.

leo: i'll run the kv-dump checksum script across archived reproductions too, maybe this is an intermittent drift that started after the shard-index patch.

olga: thanks — i'll open the issue and paste links + kv dumps now. will also attach a short diff of the failure trace and the token window.

sam: thanks team. keep thread updated. if someone finds a quick mitigant (e.g., pin rotary modulus or force cache alignment) we can push a hotfix to canary cluster.
